frequency_question: What proportion of major bills introduced and prioritized in the Senate successfully complete all required procedural steps and pass the chamber within a 293-day remaining window?
membership_rule: Includes any primary legislative bill introduced in the U.S. Senate that undergoes committee consideration and reaches floor debate/vote within a timeframe under 300 days. Excludes continuing resolutions, routine administrative bills, and omnibus packages.
provenance_note: 6 cases named, 10 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.7x)
coverage_note: 6 named prominent instances; estimated total of 10 major standalone contested votes meeting the criteria in recent comparable congressional windows.
known_gaps: Excludes bills that stall indefinitely in committee due to lack of scheduling priority.
skeleton: Legislative process steps: Committee markup (14-30 days), floor scheduling (15-45 days), debate and cloture motions (10-20 days), final passage vote (1-3 days). Minimum sequential physical duration is approximately 40 to 98 calendar days under active prioritization.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 10 major high-priority contentious bills tracked in recent sessions that moved from introduction/receipt to final Senate passage within a sub-300 day window.
validity_reason: Valid until the conclusion of the current congressional structural term, after which procedural rules or chamber majorities may shift.
